::: {.why}
The same underlying quantity becomes two different strategies depending on whether you compare a stock to its peers or to its own history, and they have different nulls, different capacities and different failure modes.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what a cross-sectional signal is neutral to by construction, and what a time-series signal is exposed to that it is not.
- Report the market beta of the same quantity traded cross-sectionally and traded as a time-series rule.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build both from last night's quantity: a cross-sectional version that goes long the top decile and short the bottom decile each day, and a time-series version that goes long or short each name against its own history. Run both through the engine and report Sharpe, market beta and gross exposure for each.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Say what the difference is: the cross-sectional version is dollar neutral by construction and its return comes from relative ordering, while the time-series version takes a net market position whose size varies. Then check whether the time-series version's Sharpe survives once you neutralise its market exposure.
:::
:::
